neighbours.label: digits of a number written inside parentheses after another value (a unit conversion '(106 degrees F)' or a year '(1801)'), as opposed to the same numbers written outside parentheses
fire: The thermometer showed 38 degrees Celsius (100 degrees Fahrenheit) at noon.
The Treaty of Utrecht (1713) ended the long war in Europe.
On the coast it was 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) by midday.
The Battle of Hastings (1066) changed the language of England.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at sea level.
The Congress of Vienna (1815) redrew the map of the continent.
In July it reached 35 degrees Celsius (95 degrees Fahrenheit) in the valley.
The Peace of Westphalia (1648) ended the Thirty Years' War.
quiet: The thermometer showed 38 degrees Celsius at noon on Monday.
The Treaty of Utrecht was signed in 1713 and ended the long war.
On the coast it was 45 degrees Celsius by midday on Friday.
The Battle of Hastings in 1066 changed the language of England.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
The Congress of Vienna met in 1815 and redrew the map.
In July it reached 35 degrees Celsius in the valley.
The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, ended the war.
